Lisa Siregar.b:
An internationally respected swimming coach, Lisa Siregar was named California Baptist University assistant coach for Rick Rowland with CBU swimming in 2003.
She has also served as the National Team coach for her native Indonesia since 1985 and has led the team to such events as the 1992, 1996 and 2000 Olympics, as well as the World Games, University Games and Asian Games.
Siregar serves as the Secretary General for the Asian Swimming Federation, and is a Vice President/Chairman of Swimming Development for Indonesia.
She was a swimmer on the Indonesian National Team from 1966-73 when Indonesia won the Asian Swimming Championships in the 70s. She set several Indonesian swimming records that have since been broken.
Siregar earned a bachelor’s degree in international business from Cal State L.A. in 1981 and a master’s degree in business administration from Northrop in 1983.
She and her husband, Chris, have three children (Rhesa, Chrisilla and Rhesi).

Jim Bossert.b:
Jim Bossert rejoined the Lancers as head coach of the men’s and women’s swimming & diving programs ahead of the 2024 season. Bossert’s debut season was one to remember as he was named the WAC Coach of the Year.
Bossert is a CBU grad, earning his Master’s Degree in Kinesiology with an emphasis in exercise science in May of 2016.
During his time away from the Lancers, Bossert gained Division I coaching experience, starting with a season in Tuscaloosa with the Alabama Crimson Tide. Following his time in the SEC, Bossert began his return west with a stint at the University of Wyoming.
With Wyoming, Bossert coached the spring group. In 2021, the men’s team finished in the top three at the WAC Championships, while the women’s team placed top four at the Mountain West Conference Championship. The season before, Bossert guided the women’s team to a top three Mountain West finish, and he also coached a male athlete that broke the 20 second barrier in the 50 yard freestyle.
Wyoming won its first conference championship in 59 years during Bossert’s first season.
After Wyoming, Bossert returned to California to be an assistant coach for the Fresno State Bulldogs.
Bossert swam collegiately at NCAA Division III Grove City College in Grove City, PA, before joining the Lancers as a graduate student in 2015. He earned his Bachelor’s Degre in Accounting from Grove City College in May 2025. He attends Verve City Church with his family.

Kevin Callister.b:
Kevin Callister joined California Baptist University as the Aquatics Director and Assistant Swim Coach in January 2019.
Prior to returning to CBU, Callister worked for the city of Moreno Valley in the Community Services Department for 12 years. Most recently, he served as Moreno Valley's Community Services Supervisor and oversaw the daily aspects of city-wide special events, sports programming, facility reservations, senior services, recreation services as well as customer service representatives. His other previous experience includes operating a local aquatic center in his home town, coaching both club and high school water polo and swim teams and officiating water polo.
Callister graduated with a Degree in Kinesiology and a minor in Psychology from CBU in 2006. He was an All-American swimmer for the Lancers in 2004, 2005 and 2006, and also served as the men's water polo captain in 2005.
He is married to Lindsey Callister, who he met at CBU. They have three children and live in Riverside, and attend Sandals Church (Palm Avenue Campus).
f: Director of Aquatics and Age Group Programs and Assistant Swim Coach
